questions.question: Barabar Cave, famously known for depicting Ashokas' inscription, is situated at_______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jehanabad district**____**, Bihar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Barabar Caves** are located in the Jehanabad district, near Gaya, Bihar.
 
• These caves are famous for their historical significance and the inscriptions of Emperor Ashoka.
 
• The caves were carved out during the Mauryan period in the 3rd century BC and are considered some of the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India.
 
• They were used by the Ajivikas, a religious sect contemporary to Buddhism and Jainism.
 
• The inscriptions in the caves provide valuable insights into the history and culture of ancient India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashoka** was the third emperor of the Maurya Dynasty and ruled almost the entire Indian subcontinent.
 
• He is remembered for his contributions to the spread of Buddhism and his efforts to govern based on Buddhist principles.
 
• The **Barabar Caves** include four caves: Karan Chaupar, Lomas Rishi, Sudama, and Visvakarma.
 
• The **Lomas Rishi Cave** is particularly notable for its elaborate entrance which is an early example of the chaitya arch.
 
• The polished surfaces and precise architecture of these caves reflect the advanced engineering skills of the Mauryan period.
 
• These caves have inspired later rock-cut architecture in India.

• **Element 106** has been provisionally named seaborgium by American researchers in honour of Nobel Laureate Glenn T. Seaborg.
 
• Glenn T. Seaborg was an American chemist whose work in the synthesis of transuranium elements earned him the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1951.
 
• Seaborgium (Sg) is a synthetic element with the atomic number 106 and is part of the transactinide series.
 
• It was first created in 1974 by a team of researchers at the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.
 
• This naming honors Seaborg's significant contributions to chemistry, particularly in the discovery of ten elements.

• It is part of the group 6 elements in the periodic table, which also includes chromium, molybdenum, and tungsten.
 
• The discovery of seaborgium was confirmed by both American and Russian teams, leading to international recognition of its name.
 
• Seaborg's work extended beyond element discovery; he also contributed to the understanding of nuclear reactions and the development of the actinide concept.
 
• The naming of seaborgium was unique because it was the first time an element was named after a living person.

• **BMI = kg/m²** is the correct formula for calculating Body Mass Index.
 
• BMI is a measure of body fat based on height and weight that applies to adult men and women.
 
• The formula divides an individual's weight in kilograms by their height in meters squared.
 
• This measurement is used to categorize individuals into various weight categories such as underweight, normal weight, overweight, and obesity.
 
• BMI is widely used by healthcare professionals to assess the risk of diseases associated with excess body fat.

• A BMI of less than 18.5 is considered underweight, 18.5-24.9 is normal weight, 25-29.9 is overweight, and 30 or greater is obese.
 
• BMI does not directly measure body fat but correlates well with more direct measures of body fat.
 
• It is important to consider other factors such as muscle mass, bone density, and overall body composition when interpreting BMI results.
 
• BMI may not be accurate for all populations, including athletes and older adults, due to differences in muscle and fat distribution.

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**
